decision.explanation: The sources confirm Donald Alexander Macdonald held multiple positions. Document 1 explicitly states he was 'Lieutenant Governor of Ontario' (D1S1, D1S2), 'member of the Canadian House of Commons' (D1S10), and implies his prior political career. Document 2 states he was a 'member of the Legislative Assembly of the Province of Canada' (D2S5), a 'special envoy to Spain' (D2S8), and a 'procurador en Cortes' (D2S2, D2S10), which is defined as a 'member of the Cortes Españolas' (D2S2, D2S10). The candidate 'Member of the Liberal Party of Canada' (C6) is rejected because the text describes him as a 'prominent figure' in the party (D1S10), not necessarily holding the specific office/position of 'Member' in the same structural sense as the other roles, though he was a member of the party. However, strictly speaking, being a 'prominent figure' does not equate to holding the position of 'Member of the Liberal Party' as a formal title like the others. The other five answers are directly supported as specific roles held.
